issues.legal_issue: A statutory order requisitioning land on the executive authority’s opinion is not reviewable by certiorari when the statute does not require the authority to decide judicially.
material_facts: The provincial government requisitioned a flat under a law authorising requisition when, in its opinion, doing so was necessary or expedient for a public purpose.

The law did not require the government to hold a hearing or determine the existence of a public purpose judicially; its provisions allowing information to be obtained and land inspected were enabling, not compulsory.
The affected occupants sought certiorari to quash the requisition order.
issues.conclusion: The requisition decision was administrative, not judicial or quasi-judicial, so certiorari was unavailable; the appeal was allowed and the petition dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the test in Rex v. Electricity Commissioners, approved in Rex v. London County Council and Ryots of Garabandho v. Zamindar of Parlakimedi, certiorari lies where a body with legal authority to determine questions affecting rights has a duty to act judicially and exceeds its authority. Whether that duty exists depends on the statute and the nature of the power. Under section 3 of the Bombay Land Requisition Ordinance, read with sections 10 and 12, the government’s determination and requisition were administrative because the Ordinance did not impose a duty to decide judicially; the optional powers to obtain information or inspect land did not change that. Franklin v. Minister of Town and Country Planning supports the distinction between an administrative decision and a judicial one. An executive authority’s determination of facts as a preliminary step to an executive function does not by itself make the decision judicial.

predicates.requisition_certiorari_proceeding: A person seeks certiorari to quash an order by an executive authority requisitioning land.
predicates.executive_opinion_controls_requisition: The governing law leaves the decision to requisition land to the executive authority’s opinion about whether doing so is necessary or expedient for a public purpose.
predicates.no_statutory_duty_to_act_judicially: The governing law does not require the authority to decide the requisition matter through a judicial process.

issues.definition: When a requisition order rests on the executive authority’s opinion and the governing law imposes no duty to decide judicially, a challenge to that order cannot proceed by certiorari.
